suggestions.title: Bed by 00:30 tonight — and log the night. The debt went up, not down.

rationale.science: At a matched calorie deficit, short sleep (5.5 h vs 8.5 h) cut fat loss by 55% and raised lean-mass loss by 60% — sleep barely changes how fast the scale moves, it changes how much of the loss comes off muscle (Nedeltcheva 2010; Wang 2018).
rationale.data: Your 7-night sleep debt is 3.8 h this morning, up from 2.8 h on Tuesday. The last two logged nights are 6.17 h (bed 01:40) and 6.00 h (bed 01:20), against 7.42 / 7.50 / 7.83 the week before. Wake is pinned at 07:30-08:00, so bedtime is the entire variable — and last night is still unlogged.
rationale.relationship: You are cutting at 0.65 %/wk with lean protection as the whole point of running it that slowly, and sleep is the only lever in the file currently pointed the wrong way. At your fixed wake time, fifty minutes of bedtime is the whole gap between a 6 h night and a 7 h one.

suggestions.predict: Bed by 00:30 puts tonight at 7.0-7.5 h. Grade it on sleep.nights gaining entries for 8/5 and 8/6, and on the 7-night debt falling under 3.0 h by Saturday. If the nights get logged and the debt still climbs, the ask is wrong and I stop making it.
